title: 5. OVARIAN CYST IN CHILDREN AND ADOLESANTS (TEENS 13 – 15 YEARS).

blocks.content:
5. OVARIAN CYST IN CHILDREN AND ADOLESANTS (TEENS 13 – 15 YEARS).

Peak incidence: 1st year of life or around menarche.

⇨Commonest cause of abdominal cyst in fetus and Neonates. More common in 3rd due to maternal Estrogen, fetal Gonadotropin, placental HCG.

Complication of Cyst:

⇨Torsion, rapture, Hge, pressure on other organs.
⇨Follicles up to 2 years of age are seen in 84%.
⇨Ovarian volume 1ml after birth.
⇨Regress spontaneously.

Types of Neoplasm in children and Adolesants:

→Benign.
→Malignant.
1.Benign:
a.Simple 60%.
b.Ovarian torsion.
c.To abscess.
d.Para tubal cyst:
-Grow large
-Don’t resolve like functional cyst.
e.Complex:
-Dermoid – 55 – 70%
-Endometrioma
-Gonad blastoma – presence of Y-chromosome.
-Serous cystadenoma
-Mucinous.

 

 

 

Dermoid:

•6 – 15years.
•10% bilateral.
•Torsion 15%.
•Malignant Transformation = 1.7%.
1.Malignant:

Sex cord stromal tumors

⇨Juvenile Granulosa cell tumors:
•50% of malignant tumors
•most common at age 6 – 13 years
•95% stage I @ diagnosis.
•>90% survival rate.
•2 – 3% B/L.
•Precocious puberty or signs of virilization are presenting symptoms.

 

Germ cell tumors

⇨Malignant ovarian Germ Cells.
•MOGCT 1.5%
•1/3 = dysgerminoma
•1/3 = immature teratoma.
•1/3 = others.
•Common in 1st 2 decades of life.
•Identified by immature neuroepithelium.

Presentation and D/D:

•Commonest symptom is pain and abdominal distention = 30%.

D/D:

•UTI – neonates commonest.
•Appendicitis – child + Adolesants.
•Gastroenteritis.
•Hirschsprung
•DKA.

 

 

⇨Acute Torsion:
•Acute pain, unilateral + vomiting + tachycardia
•In 7 – 10.5%, mean age is 9.5 – 12.5.
•Pain > 48 hours, non- migrating.
•More on righ side
•USG:
-Whirlpool sign
-Edematous ovary
-Unilateral enlargement.
-peripherally arranged follicles.

Labs:

-raised CRP
-raised TLC
-Sterile pyuria.

Treatment:

•Surgical
•Detorsion ± gonadopexy ± cystectomy.
⇨Don’t remove Blue or Black ovary (Necrotic).

Gonadopexy esp. in previous Oophorectomy or recurrent torsion.

Investigations:

⇨TAS (TVS in sexually active)

1st line.

⇨2nd line:
-MRI after 10yrs of age + sedation.
-CT before 10yrs of age without sedation.

 

 

 

 

 

Referral and presentation of ovarian cysts.

•Asymptomatic
•Pain abdomen
•Precocious puberty
•Menstrual problem

 

 

TAS

Haemorrhagic cyst

Repeat Scan after

6 – 8 weeks.

 

MDT in CA:

•Gynaecological oncologists.
•Paedriatic oncologists.
•Paedriatic surgeon.
•Paedriatic and adolescent Gynaecologist

Surgery:

•Commonly by paeds surgeon with input from Gynaecologist

 

 

 

 

Surgical tips for laparoscopy in children’s and Adolesants:

•Bladder is intraperitoneal => problem with supra pubic port.
•Urethral trauma while catheterization <10 years.
•Aorta just below skin in skinny children.

Lift up umbilicus before port insertion.

•Pneumoperitoneum @ 12 – 15mm hg in Adolesants.

8 – 10 in children.

•Port size Hernia – use 2 – 5mm port.

Close fascia > 10mm port size.

•Keep camera on while removing umbilical port due to risk of omental evisceration.
•Avoid vaginal examination and uterine manipulation.
•Limited lungs functioning due to intraperitoneal Co2 under pressure
